tasks.outcome: Open a policy file for direct editing of its raw keys and values, with a warning the first time, and leave the editor when done.

current.intent: Start raw editing of a policy file
current.system: Tells the person if neither loaded policy source is backed by a policy file; otherwise warns the first time that raw editing is for advanced users and records acceptance.

current.intent: Choose whether the user or computer policy source is edited
current.system: Offers only the sources the caller allows and returns the chosen one; leaving cancels.

current.intent: Browse the keys and values and see what can be done with the current selection
current.system: Lists keys alphabetically with sub-keys and values, and makes available only the actions that suit what is selected.
Closes the editor; every change was already applied to the loaded policy source and reaches disk only when policies are saved, whether the person finishes or leaves.

tasks.outcome: Add a new key, or a new value of a chosen kind, to a policy file.

current.system: Asks for the key name, checks it is valid and not taken under the same parent, and adds it as an empty key, selected in the list.

current.intent: Add a value to the selected key
current.system: Asks for the value name and one of five kinds, then asks for the data and stores it, replacing a value of the same name without warning.

tasks.outcome: Change the data of an existing value in a policy file.

current.system: Offers a text, number or list-of-text entry by the kind of the value, and refuses kinds such as binary.

Takes text, a list of lines, or a number within the limits of its size, shown in decimal or hexadecimal; a too-large hexadecimal number becomes the largest allowed and non-numbers change nothing. Leaving keeps the old data.
Replaces the data, keeping name and kind, and keeps the value selected.

tasks.outcome: Remove keys or values from a policy file, either leaving a deletion instruction for the machine or forgetting them entirely.

current.intent: Mark a value for deletion, or clear a key
current.system: Replaces a value with a deletion entry, or on a key offers clear everything, clear first, or delete one value by name; nothing changes until a choice is made.

current.intent: Forget a key or value completely
current.system: After confirming for a key, removes the key, its sub-keys, values and marks, or the value and its deletion entry, leaving no deletion behind.

tasks.outcome: Bring the contents of an exported set of machine settings into a policy source.

current.intent: Choose the area and start the import
current.system: Applies to the policy source of the chosen area, or from the raw editor to the file being edited, and refreshes the view afterwards.
Offers only registry files and guesses the key prefix from the first key, warning if the guess fails or the file holds default values.
Refuses without a file or prefix, loads the file and applies it directly to the policy source, saying only that it failed on any error. Leaving cancels.

tasks.outcome: Load a policy file into the user or computer policy source.

current.intent: Choose a policy file and where it applies
current.system: Reads the file and applies it to the chosen source, reporting success or that it could not be loaded; nothing reaches disk until policies are saved.

tasks.outcome: Write a policy source, or one branch of it, as an exported set of machine settings.

current.intent: Choose the area, or a branch of the file being edited, to export
current.system: Hands the policy source to the export step; a registry-backed source is first rebuilt as a policy file.

current.intent: Set the destination file, key prefix and branch
current.system: Starts the prefix from the user or computer default and the branch from the selected key; an empty branch exports everything.
Refuses without a file name, writes the branch with deletion marks, and reports success or failure. Leaving cancels.

tasks.outcome: Save a policy source out as a policy file.

current.intent: Choose the area and a file to write
current.system: Uses a policy-file-backed source as is, rebuilds a registry-backed one from the three policy locations, and reports success or that it could not be saved.
